Data on settleable particulates (dustfall) are difficult to interpret (Table II-6). Sites 1 and 2 were about 1.5 miles ENE and 0.5 miles south of the mine site, respectively. The range at site #1 was from approximately 3 to 70 tons per square mile per month; at site #2 the range was from somewhat less than 4 tons to nearly 91 tons per square mile per month. Site #3 was removed from the upwind (about 5 miles WNW) of the mine site, and was established to obtain data on background levels of settleable particulates. The highest reading at site #3 was approximately 121 tons per square mile per month; the highest values were recorded at this location, although interpretation is difficult due to the problem of algal growth in the canisters.
Topography and Physiography
The Tract II and Tract III lease areas constitute about 48 square miles of a maturely dissected upland that is part of the non-glaciated Missouri Plateau section of the northern Great Plains. The main rivers of this region, to which the streams of the lease areas are tributary, are the northward-flowing Bighorn River (about 15 miles west of Tract II) and the eastward-flowing Yellowstone River, which is the major stream of this area.
